{{Short description|Concept in mathematical category theory}}In [[category theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], a '''symmetric monoidal category''' is a [[monoidal category]] (i.e. a category in which a "tensor product" <math>\otimes</math> is defined) such that the tensor product is symmetric (i.e. <math>A\otimes B</math> is, in a certain strict sense, [[naturally isomorphic]] to <math>B\otimes A</math> for all objects <math>A</math> and <math>B</math> of the category). One of the prototypical examples of a symmetric monoidal category is the [[category of vector spaces]] over some fixed [[field (mathematics)|field]] ''k,'' using the ordinary [[Tensor product of modules|tensor product of vector spaces]].

==Definition==
A symmetric monoidal category is a [[monoidal category]] (''C'', ⊗, ''I'') such that, for every pair ''A'', ''B'' of objects in ''C'', there is an isomorphism <math>s_{AB}: A \otimes B \to B \otimes A</math> called the ''swap map''<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last1=Fong |first1=Brendan |last2=Spivak |first2=David I. |author2-link = David Spivak|date=2018-10-12 |title=Seven Sketches in Compositionality: An Invitation to Applied Category Theory |class=math.CT |eprint=1803.05316 }}</ref> that is [[natural transformation|natural]] in both ''A'' and ''B'' and such that the following diagrams commute:
*The unit coherence:
*:[[File:symmetric monoidal unit coherence.png]]
*The associativity coherence:
*:[[File:symmetric monoidal associativity coherence.png]]
*The inverse law:
*:[[File:symmetric monoidal inverse law.png]]

In the diagrams above, ''a'', ''l'', and ''r'' are the associativity isomorphism, the left unit isomorphism, and the right unit isomorphism respectively.

==Examples==
Some examples and non-examples of symmetric monoidal categories:
* The [[category of sets]]. The tensor product is the set theoretic [[cartesian product]], and any [[Singleton (mathematics)|singleton]] can be fixed as the unit object.
* The [[category of groups]]. The tensor product is the [[direct product of groups]], and the [[trivial group]] is the unit object.
*  More generally, any category with finite [[Product (category theory)|product]]s, that is, a [[cartesian monoidal category]], is symmetric monoidal. The tensor product is the direct product of objects, and any [[terminal object]] (empty product) is the unit object.
* The [[category of bimodules]] over a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] ''R'' is monoidal (using the ordinary [[tensor product of modules]]), but not necessarily symmetric. If ''R'' is [[commutative ring|commutative]], the category of left ''R''-modules is symmetric monoidal. The latter example class includes the category of all vector spaces over a given field.
*  Given a field ''k'' and a group (or a [[Lie algebra]] over ''k''), the category of all ''k''-linear [[Group representation|representations of the group]] (or of the Lie algebra) is a symmetric monoidal category. Here the standard [[tensor product of representations]] is used.
* The categories ('''Ste''',<math>\circledast</math>) and ('''Ste''',<math>\odot</math>) of [[stereotype space]]s over <math>{\mathbb C}</math> are symmetric monoidal, and moreover, ('''Ste''',<math>\circledast</math>) is a [[closed monoidal category|closed]] symmetric monoidal category with the [[Hom_functor#Internal_Hom_functor|internal hom-functor]] <math>\oslash</math>.

== Properties ==
The [[classifying space (category theory)|classifying space]] (geometric realization of the [[nerve (category theory)|nerve]]) of a symmetric monoidal category is an <math>E_\infty</math> space, so its [[group completion]] is an [[infinite loop space]].<ref>{{cite journal |author-link=Robert Wayne Thomason |first=R.W. |last=Thomason |url=http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/volumes/1995/n5/v1n5.pdf |title=Symmetric Monoidal Categories Model all Connective Spectra |journal=Theory and Applications of Categories |volume=1 |issue=5 |date=1995 |pages=78–118 |doi=10.70930/tac/pmzqeksd |doi-broken-date=7 September 2025 }}</ref>

== Specializations ==
A [[dagger symmetric monoidal category]] is a symmetric monoidal category with a compatible [[dagger category|dagger structure]].

A [[cosmos (category theory)|cosmos]] is a [[complete category|complete]] cocomplete [[Closed monoidal category|closed]] symmetric monoidal category.

== Generalizations ==
In a symmetric monoidal category, the natural isomorphisms <math>s_{AB}: A \otimes B \to B \otimes A</math> are their ''own'' inverses in the sense that <math>s_{BA}\circ s_{AB}=1_{A\otimes B}</math>. If we abandon this requirement (but still require that <math>A\otimes B</math> be naturally isomorphic to <math>B\otimes A</math>), we obtain the more general notion of a [[braided monoidal category]].
